subject: pr-127
extraction: Manually authored semantic decisions; mechanical coordinate/coverage extraction.
rationale_search: Supplied PR body and all six commit messages; full diff; relevant daemon-architecture plan; keyword search across supplied repo-rules and worktree plans. No implementation transcript located in this bounded corpus.

decisions.title: Give six caches one clearing owner
decisions.before: The TypeScript service owns six Maps and a six-call clearing list.
decisions.after: The service creates one core scope with six independent typed handles.
decisions.consequence: Core owns clearing for all six handles; TypeScript keeps the query algorithms. Five handles use symbol identities, one uses file positions. Their key and value spaces stay separate.
decisions.reason: Independent query key and value spaces are the stated reason for six handles.
decisions.intent: Explicit in the PR context, shape, and decisions.
decisions.boundary: Clearing ownership crosses into core; algorithms stay in TypeScript.

decisions.title: Empty entries before project release
decisions.before: The service synchronously clears its six Maps before starting graph release.
decisions.after: The service synchronously clears its scope before awaiting graph release.
decisions.consequence: Old cache entries disappear synchronously when release starts, even while project release is pending or rejects. The ordering is preserved; the clearing owner changes.
decisions.reason: The PR says released semantics must be unavailable while release is pending or rejecting.
decisions.intent: Explicit PR decision; existing order preserved through the core scope.
decisions.boundary: Entry eviction happens before the asynchronous project boundary.

decisions.title: Advance the cache turn only after refresh succeeds
decisions.before: beginTurn follows the awaited state refresh.
decisions.after: The ordering remains; beginTurn delegates clearing to core.
decisions.consequence: Successful refresh clears the previous turn, even for unchanged files. Failed refresh never reaches beginTurn, so it keeps the prior cache entries and query-file list. This is a cache guarantee, not a claim that every refresh side effect is rolled back.
decisions.reason: The PR says failed refresh must preserve the current successful turn.
decisions.intent: Explicit PR decision and new characterization test; behavior preserved.
decisions.boundary: The turn boundary remains after successful preparation.

decisions.title: Use a scope object at the package seam
decisions.before: Generic cache machinery is implemented inside the TypeScript service.
decisions.after: The service constructs a core helper object and calls its methods.
decisions.consequence: The service composes a core scope. The plan describes shared backend bases and inheritance; the PR shows this composed form, without giving a reason for that form. The existing TypeScript → core dependency direction is retained.
decisions.reason: The PR describes composition but gives no reason for choosing it over the plan's base/extends wording.
decisions.intent: Present in the PR shape; differs in implementation form from the plan's wording, rather than being absent from the PR.
decisions.boundary: Implementation ownership moves without moving the service class.

decisions.title: Expose reusable handles and whole-scope clearing
decisions.before: Maps are private to the service; core has no generic turn-cache surface.
decisions.after: Core exports a scope and a typed getOrCreate-only handle interface.
decisions.consequence: The public handle offers getOrCreate; scope methods clear every registered handle synchronously. Handles remain usable before beginTurn, after repeated release, and during pending project release. There is no turn gate, per-key invalidation, or handle-unregister operation; the service creates its six handles once.
decisions.reason: The public surface is stated; no reason is given for this minimal, reusable lifecycle contract.
decisions.intent: Public surface explicitly listed in PR; lifecycle limits derived from the entire new implementation.
decisions.box: Core public interface / private handle registry
decisions.boundary: Callers obtain values; scope controls typed access to clearing.

decisions.title: Pass a file list across the exported service API
decisions.before: beginTurn receives a WorkspaceSnapshot and reads snapshot.files.
decisions.consequence: The already-exported semantic service now takes a file list instead of a whole snapshot. The backend supplies snapshot.files. Direct callers of that public method must change their argument shape; the PR records the signature change without explaining why.
decisions.reason: No reason for the narrower argument is stated in the PR, commits, or relevant plan passages.
decisions.intent: Explicit PR public-surface change; not an unrequested change relative to that body.

decisions.title: Treat undefined as a cached value
decisions.before: The specialized Maps use truthiness checks on their array/promise values.
decisions.after: The generic handle tests Map.has before Map.get.
decisions.consequence: A present key is a hit even when its value is undefined. Existing TypeScript caches hold arrays or promises; the generic core contract also supports undefined without rerunning the factory.
decisions.reason: The PR explicitly names undefined as a valid cached value.
decisions.intent: Explicit PR decision; new generic behavior characterized in core.
decisions.boundary: Presence replaces truthiness in the generic cache contract.

decisions.title: Return the exact factory value between clears
decisions.before: Specialized Maps store exact array or promise objects.
decisions.after: getOrCreate stores and returns the factory result unchanged.
decisions.consequence: Between clears, a repeated key on one handle returns the same value or promise object. Clearing forgets entries without cancelling returned work. An old promise may settle later but cannot overwrite a new-turn entry. Promise identity applies at the cached service/handle boundary, not every async wrapper.
decisions.reason: The PR's compatibility intent explicitly preserves promise/value identities; it gives no separate optimization claim.
decisions.intent: Preservation explicitly requested; old-settlement consequence additionally specified by the new core test.
decisions.boundary: Entry lifetime and returned-work lifetime are distinct.

decisions.title: Keep async failures cached; retry synchronous throws
decisions.before: Rejected promises remain in the specialized Maps; a synchronous factory failure never reaches set.
decisions.after: The generic handle preserves the same split by setting only after createValue returns.
decisions.consequence: A factory that returns a promise stores it, including later rejection, until the next clear. A factory that throws synchronously stores nothing, so the next access retries. TypeScript definitions/callees take the async path; reference discovery can take the synchronous path.
decisions.reason: The stated reason is compatibility with existing failure behavior; no independent defense of the asymmetry is supplied.
decisions.intent: Explicit preservation request, with new core and TypeScript characterization tests.
decisions.boundary: Failure timing determines whether an entry exists.

decisions.title: Keep TypeScript projections and query work in place
decisions.before: The service owns query keys, observers, locations, node reconstruction, and query bodies.
decisions.after: The same work remains around getOrCreate factories and per-access projections.
decisions.consequence: Query keys and bodies stay in TypeScript. Observers run on cache misses; callers and references share cached reference locations. Position caches keep locations (including empty results), while each access rebuilds a node array. Reference results are also projected per access; the refactor does not turn all outputs into shared objects.
decisions.reason: The PR explicitly preserves all six algorithms, key spaces, and value identities.
decisions.intent: Explicit compatibility intent; position and reference projections are retained implementation choices.
decisions.boundary: Core stores generic values; language-specific reconstruction stays in the service.

decisions.title: Add contract tests while retaining prior assertions
decisions.before: The service has five tests; the generic core scope does not exist.
decisions.after: Six service tests and four core tests are added; the five prior test bodies and helpers are unchanged.
decisions.consequence: Ten new tests cover identities/isolation, empty-position projection, rejection versus throw, successful-turn preservation, immediate clearing plus awaited release, repeated release, and late promise settlement. The five existing tests remain; none is weakened or deleted. The pending/rejecting release case uses a controlled graph double. This artifact inspects tests; it does not report a test run.
decisions.reason: The PR names characterization and identity/error/clearing contracts, alongside its compatibility intent.
decisions.intent: Test additions explicitly described in PR; no removed or weakened assertions in this diff.
decisions.boundary: Generic cache guarantees gain their own tests; service contracts stay covered in their existing file.

decisions.title: Carry project completion and failure back to the backend
decisions.before: The graph's promise is started and discarded by a void service method; the backend does not await it.
decisions.after: The service becomes async and the backend awaits it, connecting the caller to graph settlement.
decisions.consequence: Backend release now waits for the graph's completion and propagates its rejection, including failure that stops later project releases. This is an observable contract change alongside the ownership move. The PR declares the barrier, but the broad plan promises unchanged failure behavior; no separate rationale reconciles that change. The generic graph already returns a promise even though concrete TypeScript cleanup is synchronous.
decisions.reason: The awaited barrier is explicit, but no separate reason reconciles changed failure/completion visibility with the plan's preservation promise. The stated clearing-order reason belongs to D02.
decisions.intent: Explicit in PR shape and public surface; broader plan tension is surfaced without a correctness verdict.
decisions.boundary: Completion/failure crosses two previously detached call boundaries.

evidence.title: PR: public surfaces
Plan: bases and language ownership
evidence.text:
### A language backend holds only language-specific logic

A concept that another language could share lives in core as a base the backend extends. The backend supplies only what depends on the language's toolchain.

```text
Shared in core: file revision tracking, prepared-file index, declarations-by-identity,
transactional index publication, project-membership graph with input invalidation,
turn-scoped query cache lifecycle.
TypeScript-only: extraction from TypeScript syntax trees, tsconfig parsing (extends,
references, path aliases, include/exclude), program and language-service creation,
semantic query bodies.
```

evidence.title: Plan: preserve behavior and separate fixes
evidence.text:
### Behavior is unchanged

This is a refactor. Every command, daemon lifecycle action, diagnostic record, telemetry event, and failure path behaves as it does today.

```text
Given the same workspace, arguments, environment, and daemon state, output bytes,
exit code, execution mode, and lifecycle outcome are identical before and after.
```

Correct: a restructuring change passes the existing e2e parity and daemon suites without touching a single expectation. Incorrect: a restructuring change "fixes" a queue, eviction, timeout, or path while moving code.

There is no "it was obviously a bug" override. Behavior defects found during restructuring are recorded in `daemon-follow-ups-functional-spec.md` and changed separately.
